_method: Families B-E, hand-authored. `contamination` records what the author had seen when writing each question, because that determines what the item can honestly prove. 'none' = derived from code bodies, which NEITHER store indexes (the structure graph holds labels and paths; the episode store holds prose) -- so retrieving the answer requires bridging intent to implementation. 'prose' = derived from README/notes that ARE indexed; these test ranking, not recall, and are marked so they are never counted as evidence of semantic ability. `expect_contains` lists strings a correct answer must mention. It replaced an earlier `expect_source` that named CODE files -- an unmeetable target, because neither store indexes code bodies. That mistake surfaced the sharpest finding in the set: docstrings and comments, where a great deal of 'why' actually lives, are invisible to both stores. Family F (`structure`) exists because the rest of this set cannot see the structure store at all: routing scores the index, and retrieval is measured with the scope forced and `with_structure=False`, so graphify is never invoked. These questions are phrased behaviourally and scored on whether the traversal surfaces the SYMBOL that answers them -- not on matching a word the question already contains. Some are known misses and are kept deliberately: a family where everything passes measures nothing.

questions.question: When entries get removed from an archive, what happens to the links that pointed at them?
questions.justification: src/zim_compress/strip_images.py:134 keeps a redirect only when its target survived; StripStats tracks copied_redirects/skipped_redirects. Question avoids the words 'redirect' and 'zim'.

questions.question: Can I drop photographs but keep vector graphics?
questions.justification: keep_svg flag in strip_images.py exempts image/svg+xml from the MIME prefix rule.

questions.question: Why would the interface load fine but stop responding to clicks on Windows?
questions.justification: app.py register_static_mime_types(): stale Windows registry mappings serve .js/.mjs with a non-JS Content-Type, so the UI loads and then fails on interaction.

questions.question: Why would the embedding model fail to load when the data directory is on a network drive?
questions.justification: app.py forces HuggingFace to copy rather than symlink: Windows cannot follow HF symlinks on a UNC share (WinError 1463), so the ONNX model fails.

questions.question: Why would a browser silently discard a login cookie that curl accepts?
questions.justification: SameSite=None without Secure is rejected by browsers per RFC 6265bis; curl does not enforce the storage rule. Documented in a vault note, so this item tests ranking not recall.

questions.question: How does someone approve a prompt without touching the keyboard?
questions.justification: tests/permissions.integration.test.ts and voice.integration.test.ts; README describes ring tap and voice. Question avoids 'glasses', 'ring' and 'voice'.

questions.question: What stops a single turn from consuming the entire budget before it produces anything?
questions.justification: Delroy's reserved landing step / step-budget work. Documented in memory notes, so marked contaminated.

questions.question: How are ZIM archive files handled?
questions.justification: TSRC manages/downloads ZIM archives; zim-compress rewrites them; tensor-serve is 'a ZIM-based retrieval augmented proxy' that builds a vector database from downloaded ZIMs. tensor-serve was missing from gold, so a correct three-scope answer scored as a precision failure.

questions.question: Which project is a self-hosted workspace for running local AI models?
questions.justification: odysseus is a self-hosted AI workspace; TSRC is offline knowledge management with local AI. Genuinely overlapping.

questions.question: Which projects deploy to Cloudflare Workers with a D1 database?
questions.justification: Both ship a wrangler.toml with a [[d1_databases]] binding: urthreads for its comment store, 3M1RY33T.github.io for portfolio-likes. Gold was ['urthreads'] alone because the second scope was registered after the item was written -- corpus drift, not a routing failure.

questions.question: Which projects ship a packaged macOS application?
questions.justification: brewery ships Brewery-v0.1.0-macOS.dmg; odysseus has build-macos-app.sh and start-macos.sh.

questions.question: Which projects extend or integrate with Claude Code?
questions.justification: g2cc mirrors a Claude Code session onto glasses; Delroy is an agent harness with Claude Code lineage.

questions.justification: no scope contains this; the router must abstain.

questions.justification: no scope contains this.

questions.justification: no discriminating vocabulary; abstaining and asking is the only correct behaviour.

questions.justification: technical and specific, but no registered scope does Kubernetes. Tests that plausibility alone does not produce an answer.

questions.justification: app/ auth dependency; the question names neither the symbol nor its file.

questions.justification: KNOWN MISS: traversal seeds on shortcode.py helpers instead of the resolver.

questions.justification: KNOWN MISS: the scope's 82-token symbol vocabulary contains none of the query terms, so expansion is empty and no traversal runs.

questions.question: which of my projects use Cloudflare workers or D1?
questions.justification: The motivating case. Before set mode this returned one owner of two: 2.098 against 1.0867, where WIDEN_RATIO needed 1.783.

questions.question: which projects use wrangler and D1?
questions.justification: The README quickstart. It returned both owners before set mode, but only by luck: `wrangler` sits in exactly two scopes and tripped CONCENTRATED_SCOPES. It is here so the luck is measured.

questions.question: which of my projects handle ZIM files?
questions.justification: Three genuine owners of one term -- the shape MAX_SCOPES=3 and the widen ratio were never sized for.

questions.question: which of my projects use Kubernetes ingress controllers?
questions.justification: Enumerative phrasing must not loosen abstention. No scope does Kubernetes; set mode drops the widen ratio and must still refuse.

questions.question: which of my projects should I work on next?
questions.justification: Enumerative frame, no discriminating vocabulary. Stripping the frame must not leave the remaining words looking like evidence.

questions.question: do any of my projects verify Stripe webhook signatures?
questions.justification: Plausible and specific, and nobody here takes payments.

questions.question: Why did short names that mix letters with numbers disappear from the search index before?
questions.justification: src/loci/text.py:24 `_WORDISH = [^\W_]+` keeps digits inside a word; the earlier `[^\W\d_]+` treated every digit as a separator AND discarded it. text.py:38 MIN_LEN_ALNUM admits two-character alphanumeric terms below the prose floor. Question names neither the constant nor the pattern.

questions.question: Why does the first question that reaches several projects at once have to load something before the parallel part starts?
questions.justification: src/loci/ask.py:207-222 pays the native initialization on one thread before the ThreadPoolExecutor fan-out; constructing the sentence-transformer concurrently returned SIGSEGV, SIGABRT and hangs. Lives in a comment, which neither store indexes.

questions.question: Why is splitting one repository into a separate entry per package not the default behaviour?
questions.justification: src/loci/scopes.py:67 WORKSPACE_MARKERS and scopes.py:177; the README explains the measurement (a new scope's alias is its bare directory name and an alias outranks cwd, 6.0 to 4.0). README is indexed, so this ranks rather than recalls.

questions.question: If someone got hold of the key for a chat later on, could they read everything that had already been sent?
questions.justification: lib/src/messages/data/encryption_service.dart:7-10 documents one STATIC X25519 keypair per session with no Double Ratchet and no forward secrecy, so a compromised key opens the whole history. Question avoids 'forward secrecy', 'ratchet' and 'key rotation'.

questions.question: Why can nothing be sent until the other person has opened the app at least once?
questions.justification: lib/src/messages/data/encryption_service.dart:19-20 throws a user-presentable MessageException when the partner has not published a public key yet; the shared secret needs both halves.

questions.question: What clears the 'still writing' indicator when a phone loses signal half way through?
questions.justification: lib/src/messages/domain/presence.dart:4-6 -- the repository's onDisconnect handler resets isOnline and isTyping when the client disappears, rather than a timeout on the reader's side.

questions.question: Can two different links differ only by which letters are capitalised?
questions.justification: app/shortcode.py:8 ALPHABET is ascii_lowercase + digits, so an uppercase letter can neither be generated nor validated -- is_valid (shortcode.py:22) rejects it outright.

questions.question: Does a caller nobody has seen before get held back on its very first rush of requests?
questions.justification: app/ratelimit.py:47 a new bucket is created with tokens=capacity, so an unseen key starts FULL and may spend the whole capacity immediately. Question avoids 'bucket', 'token' and 'capacity'.

questions.question: Could moving the machine's clock backwards get someone more requests than they are owed?
questions.justification: app/ratelimit.py:46 and :52 use time.monotonic(), which is unaffected by wall-clock changes, so refill cannot be gamed that way.

questions.question: Where does it look for the package manager on an older Mac before it gives up?
questions.justification: Sources/BreweryCore/BrewDetector.swift:26 tries /opt/homebrew/bin/brew then /usr/local/bin/brew, and :31-38 falls back to a sanitized login shell PATH before reporting not-found.

questions.question: Does this ever change what is installed on my machine without asking me first?
questions.justification: README states package actions run only after confirmation. Deictic on purpose and asked from the project root, so the working directory is the only thing that identifies the subject.

questions.question: Which commands can the glasses start on their own without waiting for approval?
questions.justification: src/daemon/tool-permissions.ts:28-29 SAFE_BASH admits a read-only set (ls, cat, head, tail, wc, pwd, stat, env, uname, and git status/log/diff/branch/show/remote/rev-parse); everything else prompts. Reworded off 'headset' and 'shell', neither of which this scope indexes -- it says `glasses` (14 nodes) throughout.

questions.question: When a tool nobody has classified reaches the glasses, is it allowed or held?
questions.justification: src/daemon/tool-permissions.ts:37-39 -- anything not in AUTO_ALLOW and not a safe Bash command returns true, i.e. unrecognized tools prompt rather than defaulting open. Reworded onto `glasses` (14) and `tool` (13); the earlier phrasing shared only `run` with the scope, so it measured the corpus rather than the router.

questions.question: If a sentence falls right on the join between two passages, is it lost to the search?
questions.justification: api/chunker.py:1 and :7 -- chunk_size 500 with overlap 50 and step = chunk_size - overlap, so consecutive passages share 50 words and a straddling sentence appears whole in one of them.

questions.question: If the same query comes back an hour later, is the whole search run from scratch?
questions.justification: api/cache.py:14 QueryCache defaults to ttl_seconds=3600 with LRU eviction past max_size=100, so an hour is exactly the boundary at which a repeat stops being free. Reworded from a phrasing whose tokens tensor-serve did not index at all -- `query` (56 nodes there) makes it reachable without naming the cache.

questions.question: Which one makes an offline archive smaller by dropping the pictures?
questions.justification: Three scopes handle ZIM archives -- zim-compress strips them, tensor-serve ingests them, TSRC browses them -- so the archive vocabulary is shared and only the VERB separates the owners.

questions.question: Which one lets me put questions to an offline archive instead of reading it?
questions.justification: Same shared ZIM vocabulary as conf-zim-shrink, resolving to the other two owners: tensor-serve serves the retrieval, TSRC is the desktop workspace that talks to it. zim-compress must NOT come back.

questions.question: Where is the write-up about the agent manager, as opposed to the tool itself?
questions.justification: _posts/2025-08-05-what-is-delroy.md and _posts/2026-07-11-introducing-delroy.md. The blog holds posts ABOUT the other projects, which is the sharpest confusion in this corpus: the post and the project share every term.

questions.question: Which one is the published site rather than the raw text that feeds it?
questions.justification: The inverse of conf-blog-writeup: MyBlog is 'raw posts from my personal website' while 3M1RY33T.github.io is the site itself. Both hold the same post vocabulary.

questions.question: Which one drops reusable coding agents into a project directory?
questions.justification: Delroy manages and deploys agents; loci and G2-claude-companion are also 'AI coding agent' tooling and share that vocabulary, so the discriminating idea is INSTALLING INTO a project.

questions.question: Where do I have code that turns text into vectors so it can be searched by meaning?
questions.justification: tensor-serve api/embedder.py and api/vectordb.py; loci src/loci/backends/episodes.py and the embeddings written by `loci embed`. Two real owners, so returning one is the failure.

questions.question: Which projects stop and ask before doing something that cannot be undone?
questions.justification: brewery runs package actions only after confirmation (Sources/BreweryCore/BrewAction.swift, README); g2cc gates every mutating tool behind a permission prompt (src/daemon/tool-permissions.ts:31-39).

questions.question: Which of my projects are written in Swift?
questions.justification: brewery is the only SwiftUI/Package.swift project in the corpus. An enumeration with exactly ONE right answer, which is the case set mode most easily over-widens on.

questions.question: Do any of my projects use Flutter?
questions.justification: hlep_davay is the only pubspec.yaml/Dart project (114 files under lib/). Same single-owner enumeration shape as enum-swift, phrased with the 'do any of' marker instead of 'which of'.

questions.question: How does the video transcoding pipeline choose a bitrate?
questions.justification: No scope transcodes video. Plausible for a corpus holding a desktop app, a worker and a media-adjacent archive tool, which is what makes it a test rather than nonsense.

questions.question: Where is the language server implemented and which protocol version does it speak?
questions.justification: No scope implements LSP. Deliberately adjacent to loci, which reasons about symbols and references and would be the tempting wrong answer.

questions.question: How are light paths sampled in the renderer?
questions.justification: No rendering code anywhere. 'renderer' collides with UI rendering vocabulary in several scopes, so the router has to refuse on evidence rather than on the word being absent.

questions.question: What decides whether one more request from the same key goes through?
questions.justification: app/ratelimit.py:17 TokenBucket.allow(key) is the decision. Avoids 'token', 'bucket' and 'limit'; reworded onto `request` and `key`, which beacon indexes, from a phrasing that shared no token with the scope at all.

questions.question: What works out which packages rely on which others?
questions.justification: Sources/BreweryCore/BrewDependencyGraph.swift holds the dependency/dependent relation the browse view renders. Question says 'rely on' rather than 'depend'.

questions.question: What sits between the message list and what the repository actually stores?
questions.justification: lib/src/messages/data/encryption_service.dart:11 is the boundary: controllers and widgets see plaintext, the repository sees ciphertext. Avoids 'encrypt'; reworded from a phrasing built on 'scrambling', a word no scope indexes, onto `message` (187) and `repository` (602), which hlep_davay does.
